schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: One parse of every .py file in the tree into an import graph, and the sieves that shake it. Three primitives: `import_graph(root)` — {relpath: every dotted name it imports}; `importers_of(graph, path)` — who imports the module at this path, the question the ruling door asks before letting a packet sentence a file; `catches(graph, rule)` — shake one sieve and return what its MESH caught. Two rule kinds, because the corpus asks two different questions: `sole_path` (these modules may be imported ONLY from inside this prefix — the domain chokepoint) and `forbidden` (this prefix may not import these at all — a fork, so one thing survives the other breaking).
why: Five artifacts had been standing on the sentence 'enforced by the tester import-scan once that tooth exists' since 2026-07-18 — db_domain's falsifier (4), inference_domain's falsifier (6), intentions_model_compiler, CLAUDE.md's rules-awaiting-physics list, and a ruling packet whose own line read 'Guarded by import-scan, never by prose'. That last one is the why in one image: the sentence asserting the rule was not prose was itself the only thing enforcing it (Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics; until it is, it is a tracked debt). THE LIVED SYMPTOM the last customer fixes: on 2026-08-05 two ruling packets sentenced cairn/base/probe.py — the Probe primitive — to deletion while 19 live modules imported it. Akien was one `cairn ruling confirm` away from making 'delete the file the corpus is built on' a green instruction, and the confirm screen shows him the READING, which was correct; nothing showed him the kill list. Both packets were caught by hand, which is the wrong mechanism twice over.
invoke: import: `from cairn.import_sieve import sieve`. Prove: `python3 cairn/import_sieve/proofs/test_import_sieve.py` (exit 0 = green). Consumers declare their own rule at their own address — db_domain/proofs/test_sole_path.py, inference_domain/proofs/test_host.py, cairn/ruling/ruling.py.
node_class: primitive (a library, not a device) — it holds no state, owns no resource, and has no face. It is read-only over the tree and returns findings; nothing here decides what to do about them.
entry: FRESH code, PROVEN pattern, promoted rather than invented. The design is inference_domain's own sole-path tooth (2026-07-21) — AST-parsed, outbound-only, matched on full dotted names, with a non-hollow floor — generalized and moved once so it stops being one component's private habit. Its two hard-won mesh lessons came from the corpus and are built in: learning_block's tooth (2026-08-01) grepped whole source and fired on its own honest docstring, fixed by scoping to import lines; inference_domain's grepped the host's port and API paths and fired on cairn/base/needs.py where ':11434/api/tags' appears in a docstring, an error message and a fixture, fixed by testing the CAPABILITY rather than the mention. Nothing crossed from outside Cairn.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why
the_mesh_is_the_whole_difficulty: A sieve is only as good as its ability to tell a capability from a mention of one, and the corpus has now taught that three times. `urllib.parse.parse_qs` is string work and no more a door than `str.split`; `urllib.request` is a door — a word-matching scan cannot separate them and web_server/server.py is the live file it would red on day one. `http.server` LISTENS; a dial rule that catches it reds the one component whose whole job is to be reachable. And a fixture STRING containing 'from cairn.base.probe import Probe' is data, not an import — measured 2026-08-06, grep counted 23 carriers of probe.py where the sieve counts 19, and all four of the difference are prose or fixtures. Hence: parse with ast, match full dotted names, never ask whether a word appears.
filed_edges: (a) A SUBPROCESS IS INVISIBLE. `subprocess.run(['curl', ...])` dials and imports nothing; so does a dynamic `importlib.import_module(computed_name)`. Every sole-path green here means 'no second door BY IMPORT', which is narrower than 'no second door'. Named rather than papered over — a green read wider than it is measured is the failure this component exists to end.

(b) THE WRITE-SCAN IS A DIFFERENT ANIMAL AND IS NOT BUILT. intentions_model_compiler's IOU is 'no second WRITER of intentions-congruency-lab/', which is a scan over a verb (open(...,'w'), write_text, shutil) and not over imports. It is one of the five customers and it is the one this component does NOT serve; its IOU stays open and is stated as still open.

(c) RELATIVE IMPORTS RESOLVE TO NOTHING. `from . import x` is skipped rather than resolved to an absolute name. Measured 2026-08-06: the corpus contains zero relative imports, so this is a real hole with no current occupant. It becomes a defect the day someone writes one.

(d) NOBODY SHAKES THE NEST. Each rule lives at its owner's address and fires under that owner's proof, which is correct (Law 5 — the constraint beside the thing it protects) and means there is no single place that reports every sole-path at once. That is a view, not an owner, and it should stay a view; when the frontier projector exists this is one of its inputs.

(e) NO CACHE, BY CHOICE. The graph is rebuilt per call — 200 files, milliseconds. A cached graph would be a scan reporting on a corpus that no longer exists, which is precisely the failure mode being closed.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_import_sieve.py, run by the tester. Every catching tooth is PAIRED: the same rule shaken over a planted graph (must catch) and over the real corpus (must not), because either half alone is satisfied by a sieve made of solid sheet metal.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a mention becomes a catch — a docstring, comment or fixture string naming a module is reported as importing it; (2) a capability escapes the mesh — urllib.request or psycopg2 imported outside its domain and NOT caught; (3) a sieve shaken over a tree it did not read reports clean instead of raising HollowScan (Law 8 — a green over zero files is not a green); (4) `importers_of` returns [] for a file that live modules import, which is the exact condition under which a ruling packet may sentence it to death; (5) an unknown rule kind returns clean rather than raising — a typo'd rule that passes forever is worse than no rule.
how_it_learns: It doesn't, and the reason is the point: this is a MESH, and a mesh that adapts is not a measurement. Its rules are declared by the components that own the constraint and change only when a human rules that the constraint changed. What DOES learn is the mesh's precision, and it learns the way Cairn's other gates do — by firing wrongly once and being narrowed, with the correction written into the code as a permanent trap rather than into someone's memory. Three such narrowings are already carried as teeth (whole-source→import-lines, port-literal→capability, word-match→full-dotted-name), each one a false red that a human adjudicated. If a fourth false red appears, the answer is a new paired tooth, never a loosened assertion.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — this is the tooth five IOUs were waiting on, and the debt was tracked as an IOU exactly as the law requires)
Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel — the sole-path scan existed in one component's proof and was about to be re-derived in a second; it lives once instead)
Law 6 (exactly one owner — a sole path IS the owner's gate; a second importer is a second door, and the gate's whole claim is that there is one)
Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass — the HollowScan raise is that law aimed at this component's own green)
Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — 'sole by construction' was a claim about the present that nothing re-checked)
owner: CC owns import_sieve's code and proofs and gates writes to them. Each RULE is owned by the component whose constraint it is — db_domain owns the 5432 mesh, inference_domain owns the dial mesh — and lives at that component's address, not here. There is deliberately no central rule registry (no-enforcer, gated ownership).
proof: proofs/test_import_sieve.py — 15 teeth (measured 2026-08-06: 15/15 green). The mesh: a parse is not a dial; listening is not dialing; prose is not an import; an in-tree leaf import is visible; an unparseable file is not a door. The floor: a sieve over one file raises rather than passing, and the real corpus clears it. The catches: sole_path catches a planted second door and is clean on the real corpus for BOTH domains; forbidden catches a fork breach and spares everyone else; an unknown kind is refused. importers_of: finds the 19 live carriers of base/probe.py, returns [] for a module nobody imports, and a module is not its own importer.
provenance: Built 2026-08-06 at Akien's direction — 'then it sounds like we do import-scan next' — the morning after a ruling pass in which the missing tooth surfaced twice: once as the gate troubles/what-dies-sentences-files-the-corpus-still-imports was owed, and once as a ruling packet claiming physics that measurably did not exist. The measurement that opened it: `import-scan` appeared nowhere in the corpus as code; every one of its occurrences was an IOU reading 'once that tooth exists'. Verified on the way in that the pattern was already proven in-house (inference_domain's tooth) rather than invented here, and on the way out with a live mutant planted at skills/_mutant_probe.py — missed by the old glob, caught by the sieve.
